schema.title: Response Dev Login Auth Dev Login Post

get.description:
The worklist (A9): one row per case with the fields the web needs, in a stable order (case id). Filters: `state` (a SQL
filter), `owner` (the opaque actor `role:user_id` or its bare user id, never a display name: F8-1), `overdue`,
`provider`, `flagged` (open watchdog flag). A patient sees only their own cases; everyone else sees all.
`risk_score` (D9) is the modelled probability of loss to follow-up, for ordering only: a patient's rows carry null.

The answer is one PAGE of at most `limit` rows (default 100, hard maximum 500; M7-7: an unbounded answer exhausted an API
pod's memory at 873,000 cases). The body is still a plain list, as before. When more rows may follow, the response
header `X-Next-Cursor` holds the cursor to send as `?cursor=` for the next page; it is absent on the last page. A page can
hold fewer than `limit` rows while a cursor is still given (the model-derived filters dropped some of the cases read,
and one request reads at most 2,000): keep following the cursor until it is absent.

post.description:
Record the confirmatory colonoscopy (demo, E8): creates a synthetic `Procedure` and
`DiagnosticReport` in HAPI for the case's patient and returns their references. The case owner
only (a primary_care_owner or specialist_owner who owns it). It appends no event: the owner
then posts `complete_confirmatory {result_ref}` and `close {evidence_ref}` with the reference.

`?completeness=` (A24, ADR-036) says how the colonoscopy ended: `complete` (default), `incomplete` or
`ct_colonography`. The report states it, and `close` accepts only a complete colonoscopy or a CT colonography.

post.description: Move the sim clock forward by `days` and/or `hours`. It never moves backwards.

Return the clock to its configured start (the demo reset).

Refused (409) once any event is dated after that start: rewinding past recorded events would
leave a log whose events lie in the clock's future, and every timer computed from it wrong.
To undo a demo, restore the database snapshot (`make demo-reset`) instead.

Approve a draft and hand it to the notification mock.

One transaction (Postgres) or one critical section (in-memory) records the approval on the
draft, appends `message_approved` as the approver and writes the outbox row, so none of the three
can exist without the others (ADR-030). Only then is the outbox drained: the notification mock
writes `message_sent` as `system:notifier` and the notification row (one transaction), or reports
why it did not (consent / contact / the case moved on): the approval stands and the response says
`sent: false`. If the drain itself fails the row stays pending, the response says so
(`blocked_reason: "pending"`) and the scheduler's next drain sends it, once.

post.description:
Reject a draft with a reason from the taxonomy (A16).

One transaction (Postgres) or one critical section (in-memory) records the rejection on the
draft and appends `message_rejected {draft_id, reason}` as the rejecting human, so neither
exists without the other and the rejection shows on the case timeline. Allowed on a frozen
case (it can only stop outreach); a closed case takes no annotation, so it answers 409.

post.description:
Written on every scheduler loop, including after a failed sweep (alive but useless is
distinguishable from dead). Not a case event.

Acquire or renew the scheduler lease for `holder` (A31). The scheduler calls it at the top of every loop: `leader: true`
with the fencing token means do the work, sending the token on each call; `leader: false` means idle and beat as a
follower. The expiry is the database's, `LEADER_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS` (default 30) after the last renewal.
Give the lease up on a clean shutdown so a follower takes over at its next loop instead of after the TTL.

schema.title: Response Release Lease Scheduler Lease Release Post

post.description:
Send every approved draft that has not gone out yet (ADR-030). The approve route drains its own
row at the end of the request; this is the safety net for an approval whose drain never ran (the
process died after the approval committed) or failed. Idempotent: a row is sent once. Counts only.
